notebook.mechanism: Weather curve, linear

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop + slope * T_out, level + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Weather curve plus night setback
notebook.verdict: seed

notebook.mechanism: On/off thermostat with hysteresis
notebook.verdict: seed

notebook.expr: where(ema(T_out, tau) < cutoff, level + slope * T_out, OFF)
notebook.mechanism: Weather curve plus summer cutoff on smoothed outdoor
notebook.verdict: seed

notebook.expr: clip(level + slope * T_out, lo, hi)
notebook.mechanism: Weather curve with min/max clamps
notebook.verdict: seed

notebook.expr: level + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room)
notebook.mechanism: Weather curve plus proportional room feedback
notebook.verdict: seed

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti)
notebook.mechanism: PI control on room temperature
notebook.verdict: seed

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off), where(T_room < sp - band, sp, sp - drop), OFF)
notebook.mechanism: Weekday/weekend schedule with a setback supply level: the controller runs a lower supply setpoint on weekends (or a different occupied window) and a higher one on weekdays, with a deadband interlock. This produces a systematic weekday-vs-weekend residual offset and a day-of-week signature.
notebook.targets: weekend_minus_weekday offset and the weekday-by-weekday residual pattern (Monday negative, Wednesday/Thursday positive), plus the midday dip
notebook.refute: If the fitted n_on/n_off are identical across weekdays and weekends, or if the weekend offset vanishes once the schedule is fit, the weekday/weekend distinction is spurious.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: parameter 'sp' has unknown type 'temp_c Banc'; known: ['clock_h', 'delta_c', 'fraction', 'gain', 'hours', 'month_n', 'slope', 'temp_c']

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off) & (T_room < sp - band), sp + boost, where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off) & (T_room > sp + band), sp - boost, OFF))
notebook.mechanism: Occupancy-scheduled thermostat with a deadband: during the occupied window the controller commands a fixed supply setpoint only when room temperature leaves a deadband around setpoint, otherwise OFF. This produces a midday OFF period when solar/internal gains push T_room above the band, and morning/evening ON pulses when it drops below.
notebook.targets: midday negative residual trough (hours 11-14) and the positive shoulder at hours 7-10 and 19-21; also the large negative residual in the >15C outdoor bands
notebook.refute: If the fitter cannot place n_on/n_off to bracket the midday dip, or if the residual trough persists after conditioning on T_room crossing the deadband, the schedule+deadband mechanism is wrong.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where(T_room < sp - band, clip(T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + ki * integral(sp - T_room, ti), sp - band, sp + band), OFF)
notebook.mechanism: PI room-temperature control with integral anti-windup and a deadband: heat is requested only when the room falls below setpoint minus deadband, and the integral term accumulates during cold mornings so the supply overshoots into midday, then shuts off when solar gains lift the room.
notebook.targets: hourly residual shape with morning ramp-up (positive at 7-10) and midday overshoot (negative at 11-14), plus the strong negative residual in warm outdoor bands
notebook.refute: If the integral time constant collapses to a very short value (behaving like pure P) or the deadband collapses to zero, the PI+deadband story is not distinguishable from simple P and should be rejected.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((ema(T_out, tau) < cutoff) & (T_room < sp - band), sp - slope * (sp - T_room) - slope * (cutoff - T_out), OFF)
notebook.mechanism: Outdoor-reset with a filtered outdoor signal and a room-temperature interlock: the controller computes a weather-compensated supply curve from a slow-filtered outdoor temperature and only enables it when the room is below setpoint minus deadband. Warm afternoons push the filtered outdoor above cutoff and disable heating, explaining the warm-band negative residuals.
notebook.targets: negative residual in the 15-20 and >20 outdoor bands and the weak correlation with outdoor temperature; also the midday dip
notebook.refute: If the fitted tau is very short (no filtering) or the cutoff sits outside the observed outdoor range, the filtered-reset mechanism adds nothing over S3 and should be dropped.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off), where(T_room < sp - band, sp, sp - drop), OFF)
notebook.mechanism: scheduled occupancy setback: during the occupied window the controller asks for a high supply setpoint when the room is below setpoint minus a deadband, and a reduced supply setpoint (setback drop) otherwise; outside the window it is OFF. The morning peak is the recovery ramp pulling the room up, the midday trough is the setback drop after recovery. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: midday negative residual trough (hours 11-14) and the morning positive residual peak (hours 7-10) in S0
notebook.refute: if the fitted occupied window does not bracket the morning positive and midday negative residual hours, or if the drop parameter collapses to zero, the setback mechanism is not what explains the residual shape
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off), level + slope * T_out, level + slope * T_out - drop + where(T_room < level + slope * T_out - drop - boost, boost, OFF))
notebook.mechanism: daytime setback with morning recovery: the controller lowers the supply setpoint during occupied midday hours (lunch/afternoon unoccupied block) and only boosts back up if the room has drifted below the setback band, producing a mid-day heat-off dip and a rebound
notebook.targets: midday negative residual trough (hours 11-14) plus the pre-dawn negative bias; the S0 residual shows a sharp dip at 11-14 that S7's simple night setback cannot produce
notebook.refute: if the fitted n_on/n_off land outside 10-15, or if the boost term never activates on held-out hours, or if held-out RMSE is not better than S7 by more than the noise band
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where(ema(T_out, tau) < cutoff, level + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room), OFF)
notebook.mechanism: weather-compensated supply with an outdoor-temperature lockout plus proportional room trim: heat is only enabled when the filtered outdoor temperature is below a lockout, and above that the supply tracks room error, so warm days shut off cleanly and mild days still modulate
notebook.targets: the strong negative residual at outdoor bands 15-20 and >20 (mean -0.65 and -1.48) and the positive residual at 10-15; S3's weather-compensation cutoff is too crude because it ignores room feedback
notebook.refute: if the fitted cutoff sits above the warmest outdoor band so the lockout never fires, or if held-out RMSE is not better than S3 by more than the noise band
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off), where(T_room > level + slope * T_out + band, level + slope * T_out - drop, level + slope * T_out), level + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: occupancy-driven supply reset: during the scheduled occupied window the controller trims the weather-compensated supply down by a fixed drop whenever the room is above the compensated target plus a deadband, otherwise it runs the full compensated curve; outside the window it runs the full curve
notebook.targets: the weekday-vs-weekend offset (weekend_minus_weekday = +0.146) and the hour-8-10 positive residual bump; a schedule that only cuts supply when the room is already warm enough would show this pattern
notebook.refute: if the fitted n_on/n_off do not bracket the weekday morning bump, or if the drop term is fit to zero, or if held-out RMSE is not better than S7 by more than the noise band
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((ema(T_out, tau) < cutoff) & ((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off)), level + slope * T_out, OFF)
notebook.mechanism: weather-compensated heating gated by both an outdoor lockout and an occupancy schedule: heat is only requested when the filtered outdoor temperature is below the lockout AND the clock is inside the occupied window, so warm afternoons and unoccupied hours both go to OFF
notebook.targets: the interaction between the outdoor-band residuals (warm bands strongly negative) and the hour-of-day residual shape; S3 alone cannot explain why the warm-band residual is so much more negative than the cold-band one
notebook.refute: if the fitted lockout never fires on held-out warm hours, or if the fitted schedule window is degenerate, or if held-out RMSE is not better than S3 by more than the noise band
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)
stop: 2 rounds without a program improving the held-out score by more than the noise band

notebook.expr: where(hysteresis(T_room, lo, hi), level, OFF)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti)

notebook.verdict: seed

notebook.expr: level + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room)
notebook.mechanism: Weather curve plus proportional room feedback
notebook.verdict: seed

notebook.expr: where(T_out > warm_cut, base + slope * T_out - warm, base + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Weather-compensated curve with a warm-weather setback: when outdoor air is mild, controller drops the supply setpoint (or shuts the boiler to a lower curve) so the building coasts, producing negative residuals exactly in the warm bands while leaving cold bands untouched.
notebook.targets: mean_by_outdoor_band: large negative residuals at 15-20 and >20 C; corr_with_outdoor weak
notebook.refute: If the fitted warm_cut lands outside the 15-20 C band, or if the warm-band residual is not explained by a single step down, the warm-weather setback hypothesis fails.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((month() >= m_start) & (month() <= m_end), base + slope * T_out + boost, base + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Seasonal changeover with a shoulder-season boost: the controller runs a different (higher) curve during the heating-season months and a lower curve in the shoulder months, mimicking a manual seasonal reset or a calendar-driven schedule.
notebook.targets: mean_by_month: strong negative April, positive October; seasonal asymmetry
notebook.refute: If m_start and m_end do not bracket a contiguous block that matches the sign flip between April and October, or if the boost is not significant, the seasonal-changeover hypothesis fails.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= eve_on) | (hour_of_day() < eve_off), base + slope * T_out + evening, base + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Occupancy-driven evening warm-up plus midday setback: controller raises supply during an evening occupancy block and lowers it during a midday unoccupied block, on top of the weather curve.
notebook.targets: mean_by_local_hour: positive spike at 19-20, negative dip at 13-14
notebook.refute: If the fitted evening window does not straddle hours 19-20, or if the midday dip cannot be captured by the same window's complement, the occupancy-schedule hypothesis fails.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where(T_room < sp, base + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti), base + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Weather-compensated feedforward with a room-temperature PI trim that only engages when the room is below setpoint: the boiler curve is the baseline, and a room-sensor PI loop adds heat only on the cold side, so residual sign tracks room state rather than outdoor alone.
notebook.targets: residual structure not captured by pure feedforward: corr_with_humidity, weekday pattern, night/weekend differences
notebook.refute: If kp and ti both fit to zero, or if the conditional PI term does not reduce residual variance beyond S1, the trim-loop hypothesis fails.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where(ema(T_out, tau) > warm_off + warm_band, OFF, base + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: outdoor-reset with a smoothed outdoor lockout: heating is disabled once a slow exponential filter of outdoor temperature crosses wipeout, so brief warm spells do not shut the boiler but sustained warmth does
notebook.targets: large negative residuals at T_out > 15 C (mean -0.36 and -0.86); the controller stops heating above a filtered outdoor threshold rather than a raw one
notebook.refute: if the fitted tau collapses to near zero (making it identical to a raw-T_out cutoff already tested as M1.1) or if the warm-band region is not where the residual mass sits
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: ema: second argument must be a parameter of type 'hours'

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= eve_on) | (hour_of_day() < eve_off), base + slope * T_out + evening, base + slope * T_out) + slope * (T_out - ema(T_out, tau))
notebook.mechanism: evening setpoint boost combined with an anticipatory term driven by the difference between instantaneous and filtered outdoor temperature (a reset curve that leads the weather)
notebook.targets: positive residuals at hours 19-20 (+0.06, +0.12) and the small negative bias at hours 13-17; also the weak corr_with_outdoor (-0.08)
notebook.refute: if the fitted evening window is empty or the tau term adds no held-out improvement over S7 alone
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((month() >= m_start) & (month() <= m_end), base + slope * T_out + boost, base + slope * T_out) + slope * (T_out - ema(T_out, tau))
notebook.mechanism: shoulder-season changeover: the controller runs a different reset curve (with a boost) during the shoulder months, plus an outdoor-anticipation term; this is the classic 'summer/winter changeover' schedule
notebook.targets: monthly residual pattern: -0.23 in April, +0.16 in October, near zero in May and September
notebook.refute: if the fitted month window is empty or covers the whole year, or if the boost is not significantly different from zero
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= day_on) & (hour_of_day() < day_off), base + slope * T_out, base + slope * T_out - night_drop) + slope * (T_out - ema(T_out, tau))
notebook.mechanism: occupancy schedule with night setback (lower supply at night) plus an outdoor-anticipation term; the day window is the occupied period and the setback explains the early-morning negative bias
notebook.targets: hourly residual shape: negative bias 13-17, positive bias 19-20, and the weekday-3 positive residual (+0.15)
notebook.refute: if the fitted day window is empty or if the night_drop is not significantly different from zero, or if the anticipation term does not improve held-out RMSE over S7
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where(ema(T_out, tau) > warm_off + warm_band, OFF, base + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Outdoor-reset supply curve with a warm-weather lockout: the controller tracks a filtered outdoor temperature and shuts the boiler off entirely once that filtered value rises above a threshold (with a small band), so no heat is delivered on mild days even though the reset curve would otherwise call for a low supply temperature. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: warm-weather residual: large negative mean residual in the 15-20 and >20 outdoor bands, and the negative April/October month means
notebook.refute: If adding the filtered-outdoor lockout does not reduce held-out RMSE relative to S1, or if the fitted warm_off/warm_band land outside the range where the 15-20 and >20 bands actually occur (i.e. the lockout never fires on the held-out data), the mechanism is refuted.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)
stop: 2 rounds without a program improving the held-out score by more than the noise band

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where((hour_of_day() >= (n_on - lead)) & (hour_of_day() < n_on), boost, OFF)
notebook.mechanism: Optimum-start / recovery boost: the controller raises supply temperature for a lead window before the occupied period begins, producing a pre-heat overshoot that a plain PI cannot reproduce.
notebook.targets: the morning positive residual bump (hours 2-8, peak ~0.09) and the evening positive bump (hours 18-22, peak ~0.115) in mean_by_local_hour
notebook.refute: If the fitted lead window collapses to zero or the boost is zero, or if the hourly residual pattern is unchanged, there is no pre-heat boost.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: unknown name 'n_on'

notebook.expr: clip(T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti), tmin, tmax)
notebook.mechanism: Supply-temperature saturation: the commanded supply is clipped at a maximum (boiler/valve limit) and a minimum (condensing floor), so in mild weather the room cannot track the setpoint and the model over-predicts heat.
notebook.targets: the large negative residual at high outdoor temperature (bands 15-20 and >20, -0.17 and -0.28) where the loop cannot deliver enough heat, and the small positive bias at low outdoor temperature
notebook.refute: If the fitted clip bounds are wide enough that clipping never activates on the held-out data, saturation is not the cause of the warm-weather residual.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: parameter 'ti' has unknown type 'hoursbef'; known: ['clock_h', 'delta_c', 'fraction', 'gain', 'hours', 'month_n', 'slope', 'temp_c']

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp + reset * (t_ref - T_out) - T_room) + integral(sp + reset * (t_ref - T_out) - T_room, ti)
notebook.mechanism: Outdoor-reset PI: the supply setpoint is shifted up when it is cold outside and down when it is warm, so the loop overshoots in mild weather and undershoots in cold weather relative to a fixed-setpoint PI.
notebook.targets: residual correlation with outdoor temperature (-0.161) and the monotone drift in mean_by_outdoor_band (positive below 10C, strongly negative above 15C)
notebook.refute: If the fitted reset slope is indistinguishable from zero, or if adding it does not reduce the held-out RMSE below S4, the residual-vs-outdoor structure is not a setpoint reset.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off), sp_day, sp_night) - T_room) + integral(where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off), sp_day, sp_night) - T_room, ti)
notebook.mechanism: Scheduled setback PI: a lower night setpoint and higher day setpoint, with the loop lagging the schedule so the room runs warm at the end of the night and cool in the afternoon.
notebook.targets: the negative daytime residual (hours 9-16, ~-0.04) and the positive overnight residual (hours 19-23 and 2-8), plus the small weekday pattern in mean_by_weekday
notebook.refute: If the fitted day and night setpoints coincide, or if the residual-by-hour shape is not improved over S4, there is no setback schedule.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where((hour_of_day() >= (n_on - lead)) & (hour_of_day() < n_on), boost, OFF)
notebook.mechanism: PI room control with an anticipatory morning boost: the controller raises supply temperature for a lead-time window before the scheduled occupancy start, producing a pre-heat that the plain PI loop misses. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: positive residual in late evening hours (20-22) and the pre-dawn warm-up bump (3-6)
notebook.refute: If the fitted lead collapses to zero or the boost parameter goes to zero, or if adding the boost window does not reduce the hour-of-day residual amplitude, the pre-heat mechanism is not supported.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: clip(T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti), tmin, tmax)
notebook.mechanism: PI room control whose output is bounded by a supply-temperature limit: the integral term saturates against a high or low clamp, so the loop cannot fully correct the room error in mild weather, leaving a temperature-dependent residual. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: residual bias that grows with outdoor temperature (negative at >15C, positive at <10C) and the month-10 positive offset
notebook.refute: If the fitted clamps sit far outside the observed supply range (so clipping never activates) or if the outdoor-band residual is unchanged, the saturation mechanism is not the explanation.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off), sp, sp - night_drop) - T_room) + integral(where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) & (hour_of_day() < n_off), sp, sp - night_drop) - T_room, ti)
notebook.mechanism: PI control on room temperature with a scheduled setback: the controller tracks a lower setpoint overnight and a higher setpoint during occupied hours, so the supply temperature is systematically higher than S4 predicts in the early-morning recovery and evening pull-down, and lower in the afternoon when the room is already near setpoint
notebook.targets: residual mean_by_local_hour: positive at 03-06 and 19-22, negative at 11-15; the diurnal shape that S4 (constant setpoint) cannot produce
notebook.refute: if the fitted n_on/n_off collapse to the same value (no schedule) or the held-out RMSE is not better than S4 by more than the noise band, the residual diurnal shape is not a setback schedule
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp + reset * (t_ref - T_out) - T_room) + integral(sp + reset * (t_ref - T_out) - T_room, ti)
notebook.mechanism: outdoor-reset PI: the effective setpoint is raised as outdoor temperature falls (reset slope on T_out), so supply is hotter than a fixed-setpoint PI in cold weather and cooler in mild weather. M1.1 tried this but coupled reset to the integral too; here reset only shifts the proportional setpoint, which is the common commercial form
notebook.targets: residual mean_by_outdoor_band: strongly negative at >15 and 15-20, positive at 5-10 and <0; corr_with_outdoor = -0.161
notebook.refute: if the fitted reset slope is near zero, or held-out RMSE is not better than S4, outdoor reset is not the missing mechanism
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + where((hour_of_day() >= (n_on - lead)) & (hour_of_day() < n_on), boost, OFF)
notebook.mechanism: optimal-start pre-heat: the controller raises supply above the PI demand for a lead window before the morning occupancy start, and again before the evening occupancy start, producing extra heat exactly in the hours where S4 under-predicts. M1.1r used a single lead window and was refuted; this version uses the same lead for both morning and evening starts via a single n_on and lead, which is the standard two-event optimal-start form
notebook.targets: residual mean_by_local_hour positive peak at 03-06 (pre-dawn warm-up) and the small positive at 19-22
notebook.refute: if the fitted lead is zero or the boost window does not align with the positive residual hours, optimal-start pre-heat is not the cause
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: T_room + kp * (sp - T_room) + integral(sp - T_room, ti) + wind_gain * (T_out - ema(T_out, wind_tau))
notebook.mechanism: feed-forward on outdoor-temperature rate of change: many controllers add a term proportional to the filtered derivative of outdoor temperature (or equivalently a fast-minus-slow outdoor signal) to anticipate load changes during weather fronts, which shows up as a residual correlated with the high-frequency component of T_out rather than its level
notebook.targets: residual corr_with_outdoor = -0.161 and the month effect (October +0.141 vs September -0.042) that a pure outdoor-reset cannot capture; also the >20 band negative bias
notebook.refute: if the fitted wind_gain is near zero or the improvement is within the noise band, no rate-of-change feed-forward is present
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room), level + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room))
notebook.mechanism: Outdoor-reset base supply plus proportional room feedback with a setback schedule. The room loop closes the gap when the room is cold (early morning, evening) and backs off when the room is warm (midday solar gain), producing the sign-flipped diurnal residual that pure open-loop reset cannot explain.
notebook.targets: fireplace hour-of-day residual shape (positive early morning, negative midday/afternoon, positive late evening) and tv evening positive residual
notebook.refute: If kp fits to zero, or if adding the room term does not reduce the hour-of-day residual amplitude compared to S7, the proportional-feedback mechanism is not supported.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: unknown name 'kp'

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop + slope * T_out, level + slope * T_out) + integral(sp - T_room, tau)
notebook.mechanism: Scheduled outdoor-reset plus a slow integral trim on room temperature error. The integral term accumulates over hours to days, so weekday occupancy patterns and seasonal drift in room temperature bias the supply in a way that a static schedule cannot capture.
notebook.targets: fireplace weekday effect (Wednesday/Thursday positive) and the slow month-scale drift (April negative, October positive)
notebook.refute: If the integral time constant fits to a value shorter than the diurnal cycle (so it behaves like proportional feedback and duplicates H2), or if weekday/month residuals do not shrink, the slow-integral-trim mechanism is not supported.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: unknown name 'sp'

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room), level + slope * T_out + kp * (sp - T_room))
notebook.mechanism: Scheduled setback with proportional room feedback: the controller lowers the supply setpoint during the unoccupied window and adds a proportional correction on the room error, so the supply tracks both outdoor temperature and how far the room is from setpoint. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: hour-of-day residual shape in fireplace and tv, plus the room-temperature feedback term that S7 lacks
notebook.refute: If kp fits to zero or the fitted n_on/n_off collapse to a single window that makes the two branches identical, the schedule-plus-proportional mechanism is not supported.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: 7 parameters, cap is 6

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop + slope * T_out, level + slope * T_out) + integral(sp - T_room, ti)
notebook.mechanism: Scheduled setback combined with integral room-error trim: the schedule sets the base supply, and an integral term on the room error slowly corrects persistent offset. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: slow drift and hour-of-day residual that a pure schedule cannot explain
notebook.refute: If the integral term drives the fit worse than the schedule alone, or the fitted ti saturates at the bound, the integral-trim mechanism is not supported.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: integral: second argument must be a parameter of type 'hours'

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop + slope * ema(T_out, tau), level + slope * ema(T_out, tau))
notebook.mechanism: Outdoor reset schedule with night setback, but the controller uses a filtered outdoor temperature (sensor lag or deliberate averaging) rather than instantaneous T_out. When outdoor air warms quickly in spring/afternoon, the filtered value lags, so supply stays higher than the instantaneous-reset model predicts, producing the sign pattern seen in the warm bands.
notebook.targets: fireplace mean_by_outdoor_band: large negative residuals at 15-20 and >20 C, plus the hour-of-day morning/evening asymmetry
notebook.refute: If the fitted tau collapses to near zero, or if the residual by outdoor band does not flatten (the >20 C bias persists), the lagged-outdoor-reset explanation fails.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), clip(level + slope * T_out, lo, hi), OFF)
notebook.mechanism: Outdoor-reset with a high-limit cutoff: the controller stops calling for heat entirely once outdoor air exceeds a lockout threshold, and clamps supply at a minimum when very cold. This is the standard boiler outdoor-reset curve with warm-weather shutdown, which the linear S1 cannot represent.
notebook.targets: fireplace and tv outdoor-band residuals at the warm end (>20 C, 15-20 C) where the model over-predicts heat, and the near-zero heat_on_share
notebook.refute: If the fitted hi lands above the warmest observed T_out (so the clip never binds), or if the warm-band residual is unchanged, the warm-weather-shutdown hypothesis is refuted.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop * where(weekday() < wk, fraction, fraction) + slope * T_out, level + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Weekday-dependent setback depth: the controller uses a different setback or setpoint on some weekdays (e.g. a mid-week occupancy schedule), so the supply differs by day of week even at the same hour and outdoor temperature.
notebook.targets: fireplace weekday pattern (Wed +0.15, Tue +0.06, Mon -0.05) and tv Tue/Wed positive residual; weekend_minus_weekday is small but weekday means are not flat
notebook.refute: If the fitted weekday split collapses to a single group (wk at a bound) or the per-weekday residual spread does not shrink, the weekday pattern is noise.
notebook.verdict: rejected by validator: unknown name 'fraction'

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop + slope * T_out + kp * (T_room - T_out), level + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Scheduled setback with a proportional boost toward the room when the room is cold relative to outdoor — a weather-compensated controller that also reads room temperature during the occupied window. The (T_room - T_out) term makes the supply rise when the room lags outdoor, which is exactly the morning warm-up and evening recovery shape.
notebook.targets: fireplace residual: positive morning hours 5-10, negative afternoon 13-18, and negative >15C outdoor band; also tv evening positive 17-22
notebook.refute: If kp fits to ~0 or the held-out RMSE is not better than M1.3, the room-feedback term is not doing the work and the residual is purely schedule/weather.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on - tau) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop + slope * T_out, level + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: Optimal-start / early morning boost: the controller begins the occupied setpoint a few hours before the scheduled hour, so the supply is elevated during the pre-dawn hours and drops earlier in the afternoon than a fixed schedule would. tau is the early-start lead time.
notebook.targets: fireplace morning ramp 5-10 (positive residual) and the sharp sign flip at hour 12-13; tv evening 17-22 positive residual
notebook.refute: If the fitted tau is at the bound near zero, or the improvement over S7 is inside the noise band, the residual is not an early-start artifact.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where(((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off)) & (T_out < cutoff), level + slope * T_out, OFF)
notebook.mechanism: Outdoor-air lockout: the boiler is disabled above a cutoff outdoor temperature even during scheduled hours. Explains why the model over-predicts heat in mild weather and why the residual is most negative exactly in the warm bands.
notebook.targets: fireplace negative residual in 15-20 and >20 outdoor bands (heat off when warm); tv negative residual in >20 band
notebook.refute: If the fitted cutoff lands above the warmest observed outdoor temperature (lockout never triggers), or if RMSE in the 15-20 and >20 bands does not improve, the warm-band residual is not a lockout.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)

notebook.expr: where((hour_of_day() >= n_on) | (hour_of_day() < n_off), level - drop * where(weekday() < wk, wk, wk) + slope * T_out, level + slope * T_out)
notebook.mechanism: A scheduler with a separate weekday/weekend (or per-day) setback depth: the night/day setback is deeper on weekdays than weekends, so the effective supply offset during the unoccupied window depends on the day of week rather than being a constant drop. (repaired after validator rejection)
notebook.targets: weekday-vs-weekend and day-of-week structure in the residual of the best schedule+outdoor program (M1.3), which uses a single setback depth for all days
notebook.refute: If the fitted weekday/weekend split collapses (wk at a bound, or drop*wk indistinguishable from drop), or held-out RMSE does not improve over M1.3 beyond the noise band, the day-of-week modulation of setback is not supported.
notebook.verdict: refuted (worse than best by more than the noise band)
